(Nir. vii, 12) स्नायति (ep. also Ā. स्नायते Pot. स्नायात्; ep. also स्नायीत; pf. सस्नौ, 3. pl. सस्नुः, MBh.; BhP.; fut. स्नाता Gr.; स्नास्यति, ˚ते, MBh. &c.; aor. अस्नासीत् Gr.; Prec. स्नायात् [cf. above] or स्नेयात्, ib.; inf. स्नातुम्, Br. &c.; ind.p. स्नात्वा, -स्नाय, RV. &c.; Ved. also स्नात्वी, Pāṇ. vii, 1, 49), to bathe, perform the ceremony of bathing or certain prescribed oblations (esp. on returning home from the house of a religious preceptor, or on concluding certain vows &c., also with अवभृथम्), RV. &c. &c.; to smear one's self with (instr.), Sarvad. : Pass. स्नायते (aor. अस्नायि impers.), Rājat. : Caus. स्नापयति or स्नपयति, (with prep. only स्नाप्˚), to cause to bathe, wash, cleanse, AV. &c. &c.; to wash away, AV. x, 1, 9; to steep or soak in (loc.), Bhpr.; to bathe with tears, weep for (?), MW. : Desid. सिस्नासति, Pāṇ. viii, 3, 61 (but cf. सिष्णासु) : Intens. सास्नायते, सास्नाति, सास्नेति Gr.
स्ना [cf. Gk. νάω, νᾶμα; Lat. nare.]
2. स्ना (or ष्णा) mfn. bathing, bathed or immersed in (cf. घृत-, सु-स्ना &c.)
a: स्ना — {c2c} P. (स्नाति, स्नात) 1 To bathe, perform ablution; मृगतृष्णांभसि स्नातः. --2 To perform the ceremony of bathing at the time of leaving the house of one's spiritual preceptor. --Caus. (स्नापयति-ते, स्नपयति-ते) To cause to bathe, wet, moisten, sprinkle; (तोयैः) सतूर्यमेनां स्नपयांबभूवुः Ku. 7. 10; स्मितस्नपिताधरा Gīt. 12, U. 3. 23, Ki. 5. 44. 47; Śi. 2. 7, Me. 43. --Desid. ( सिस्नासति) To wish to bathe. -WITH अप to bathe after mourning. --नि to plunge deep into; i. e. to be perfect or thoroughly versed in; see निष्णात.

gAtrARi sarvvaM pApaM pramocaya । namaste sarvvaBUtAnAM praBavAriRi suvrate ॥” * ॥ namo nArAyaRAya ityazwAkzararUpamUlamantreRa caturasraM catuzkoRarUpaM samantataH sarvvadikzu caturhastaM jalaM m: स्नान n. (ifc. f(आ). ) bathing, washing, ablution, religious or ceremonial lustration (as of an idol &c.), bathing in sacred waters (considered as one of the six daily duties [cf. षट्-कर्मन्] or as an essential part of some ceremonial, esp. the ablutions performed by a Brahma-cārin on becoming a householder, cf. स्नातक), GṛŚrS.; Mn.; MBh. &c. (IW. 242; RTL. 394 n. 1 &c.)
washing off, removal by washing, cleansing, BhP.
anything used in ablution (e.g. water, perfumed powder &c.), Kāv.; VarBṛS.; Vet.; BhP.
a: स्नानं — [स्ना-भावे ल्युट्] 1 Bathing, washing, ablution, immersion in water; ततः प्रविशति स्नानोत्तीर्णः काश्यपः Ś. 4. --2 Purification by bathing, any religious or ceremonial ablution. --3 The ceremony of bathing or anointing an idol. --4 Anything used in ablution. --Comp. --अगारं a bath-room. --तृणं Kuśa-grass. --द्रोणी a bathing tub. --यात्रा the festival held on the full-moon day in the month of Jyeṣṭha. --वस्त्रं a bathing-garment; सकृत् किं पीडितं स्नानवस्त्रं मुंचेत् द्रुतं पयः H. 2. 106. --विधिः {1} the act of ablution. {2} the proper manner or rules of ablution.

m: स्नातक m. one who has bathed or performed ablutions (i.e. a Brāhman who, after performing the ceremonial lustrations required on his finishing his studentship as a Brahma-cārin under a religious teacher, returns home and begins the second period of his life as a Gṛha-stha See समावर्तन; three kinds of Snātakas are named, 1. a विद्या-स्न्˚, q.v., 2. a व्रत-स्न्˚ [who has completed the vows, such as fasting, continence &c., without the Vedas], 3. a विद्या-व्रत-स्न्˚ or उभय-स्न्˚ [who has completed both Vedas and vows], the last is the highest; in a wider sense there may be 9 Snātakas See Mn. xi, 1), ŚBr.; GṛS.; Gaut.; Mn. iii, 4 &c. (IW. 296).
a: स्नातकः — 1 A Brāhmaṇa who has performed the ceremony of ablution which has to be performed on his finishing his first Āśrama (that of a Brahmacārin). --2 A Brāhmaṇa just returned from the house of his preceptor and become an initiated householder (गृहस्थ). --3 A Brāhmaṇa who is a Bhikṣu (beggar of alms) for any religious object; Ms. 11. 2. --4 Any man of the first three classes who is an initiated householder.
